diffs.evidence: The second reading's 0.01 scale / 0 offset is the OUTPUT format of bmp280_compensate_T_int32 ("Returns temperature in DegC, resolution is 0.01 DegC. Output value of '5123' equals 51.23 DegC"), not a conversion of the raw 20-bit adc_T register value at 0xFA. The model maps raw adc_T via datasheet sec. 8.1 bmp280_compensate_T_double: var1 = (adc_T/16384.0 - dig_T1/1024.0)*dig_T2; T = (var1+var2)/5120.0. With the simulator's calibration registers (dig_T1 = 0x6B70 = 27504, dig_T2 = 0x6743 = 26435, dig_T3 = 0 so var2 = 0) this is exactly linear: scale = 26435/16384/5120 = 0.00031512975692749 degC/count, offset = -27504/1024*26435/5120 = -138.67726135253906 degC, matching part.json to full precision. The driver implements the same datasheet formula, and check.ts passes the simulator test (31.40 C).

diffs.diff: pressure_Pa: datasheet reading gives 0.00390625 per count, the part's model has 0.0003151, -0.001666
diffs.evidence: 0.00390625 = 1/256 is the OUTPUT format of bmp280_compensate_P_int64 ("Returns pressure in Pa as unsigned 32 bit integer in Q24.8 format... Output value of '24674867' represents 24674867/256 = 96386.2 Pa"), not a scale for the raw adc_P register at 0xF7. (0.0003151 in the diff is the temperature scale, compared against it by mistake.) The model maps raw adc_P in hPa via sec. 8.1 bmp280_compensate_P_double: p = (1048576 - adc_P - var2/4096)*6250/var1; p += (dig_P9*p*p/2^31 + p*dig_P8/32768 + dig_P7)/16. With the simulator's calibration (dig_P1 = 36477, dig_P4 = 2855, dig_P7 = 15500, dig_P8 = -14600, dig_P2/P3/P5/P6/P9 = 0) the result is linear and does not depend on temperature: scale = -6250/36477*(1 - 14600/524288)/100 = -0.0016656946671206 hPa/count, offset = ((1048576 - 2855*65536/4096)*6250/36477*(1-14600/524288) + 15500/16)/100 = 1680.2060188766 hPa, matching part.json exactly. The negative scale is correct (pressure falls as adc_P rises). The driver uses the same formula and the simulator test (950.00 hPa) passes.
